title: Creative diversity: Individual gains can homogenise groups
desc: Separates output quality from collective diversity and treats personas as preliminary mitigation rather than a proven solution.

kps.k: AI can improve individual creative output while narrowing collective diversity; the two outcomes require separate assessment.
kps.d: Doshi and Hauser’s preregistered experiment with 293 writers found that access to GPT-4 starting ideas increased evaluated story novelty by 6.7% and usefulness by 6.4%, while making stories more semantically similar. Writers with lower baseline Divergent Association Task scores benefited most. The Cybernetic Teammate likewise reports performance gains alongside greater similarity in product-development solutions. These findings distinguish better individual outputs from a broader collective range of ideas, rather than treating either as a complete measure of creativity or organisational benefit.

qs.q: We find that the provision of AI ideas improves the story’s novelty by 6.7% (b=0.259, p=0.001, see Table S3; compared to the Human only mean of 3.85) and its usefulness by 6.4% (b=0.319, p<0.001; compared to the Human only mean of 5.02).
qs.a: Generative AI Enhances Individual Creativity but Reduces the Collective Diversity of Novel Content · Academia · 2024

qs.q: While human-only solutions (both individual and pair) show relatively dispersed distributions, AI-aided solutions demonstrate notably higher semantic similarity.
qs.a: The Cybernetic Teammate: A Field Experiment on Generative AI Reshaping Teamwork and Expertise · Academia · 2025

kps.k: Homogenisation is not a uniform finding: exposure settings and input design may change the direction of diversity effects.
kps.d: Ashkinaze and colleagues studied passive exposure to examples in a dynamic alternative-uses task, with earlier responses feeding into later trials. Among 844 participants, high AI exposure increased collective diversity relative to control, with Cliff’s delta of 0.31 when disclosed and 0.26 when undisclosed, but did not improve average individual originality. Control ideas converged over time; high-exposure conditions had more positive diversity trajectories. The authors propose that AI examples interrupt human convergence. Wan and Kalman instead explain homogenisation through similar inputs generated from uniform prompts. These accounts challenge inevitability without directly contradicting experiments using different tasks and interaction designs; neither establishes a general cognitive mechanism.

qs.q: Most notably, exposure to AI ideas did not, on average, make human                                                                        ideas any ‘better’ or ‘worse’ (by creativity).
qs.a: How AI Ideas Affect the Creativity, Diversity, and Evolution of Human Ideas: Evidence From a Large, Dynamic Experiment · Academia · 2024

qs.q: From this perspective, the observed reduction in diversity may be less about inherent limitations of GenAI and more about the speciﬁc, non-interactive way in which it was implemented in this one particular study.
qs.a: Diverse AI Personas Can Mitigate the Homogenization Effect in Human-AI Collaborative Ideation · Academia · 2025

kps.k: Diversified AI personas offer preliminary mitigation evidence, not a demonstrated solution to the quality–diversity trade-off.
kps.d: Wan and Kalman generated 300 plots through ten personas and found greater variation between personas than within them. Their subsequent analysis of 97 human stories compared diversified assistance with unaided writing. The replication analysis found no significant similarity differences; mixed-effects modelling found reduced similarity with one plot but not five. Reported power was only 55.4%, and comparisons with control did not establish equivalence. The authors interpret the pattern as promising mitigation, while leaving unresolved whether diversified assistance preserves the individual creativity gains found by Doshi and Hauser. Richer descriptive and emotional vocabulary does not settle that question.

qs.q: Our analysis demonstrates robust persona distinctiveness in AI persona-generated plots, with mean intra-persona similarity of 87.41 (SD = 3.17) signiﬁcantly exceeding inter-persona similarity of 82.93 (SD = 3.12).
qs.a: Diverse AI Personas Can Mitigate the Homogenization Effect in Human-AI Collaborative Ideation · Academia · 2025

qs.q: 3.3 Phase 2 Results and Discussion 3.3.1 Collective diversity of stories by GenAI-aided human participants increased e replication analysis results indicated no signiﬁcant diﬀerence in story similarity across conditions (1-plot condition: b = -0.493, p = 0.301; 5-plot condition: b = -0.356, p = 0.459, see Table 2).
qs.a: Diverse AI Personas Can Mitigate the Homogenization Effect in Human-AI Collaborative Ideation · Academia · 2025

kps.k: Extensive retention of AI text does not establish passive copying or eliminate human creative contribution.
kps.d: In The Cybernetic Teammate’s experiment with 776 P&G professionals, AI-assisted individuals and teams improved performance by 0.37 and 0.39 standard deviations over unaided individuals, compared with 0.24 for unaided teams. The authors interpret this as partial substitution for collaborative functions, not wholesale replacement. Participants whose final solutions contained entirely AI-generated content averaged 23.9 prompts; assisted outputs remained closer semantically to human-only than AI-only outputs. This supports an interpretation of active shaping, although prompt counts do not prove critical checking and the paper inconsistently describes its AI-only comparator. Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier associates greater retention with better answers, but does not establish retention as the cause; its supplied excerpt describes a diversity method without reporting diversity results.

qs.q: Individuals working with AI showed a substantial 0.37 standard deviation performance increase over the baseline of working alone without AI.
qs.a: The Cybernetic Teammate: A Field Experiment on Generative AI Reshaping Teamwork and Expertise · Academia · 2025

qs.q: Either way, what is clear is that those who choose to retain to a relatively high degree produced significantly better answers on average, and that this certainly can have a profound impact on how organizations consider the use of GenerativeAI technologies by their employees.
qs.a: Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier: Field Experimental Evidence of the Effects of AI on Knowledge Worker Productivity and Quality · Academia · 2023

kps.k: Creation tasks look more promising for human–AI collaboration than predefined-choice decisions, but gains are not guaranteed.
kps.d: When Combinations of Humans and AI Are Useful reports average performance losses from combining humans and AI, while distinguishing task types. Decision tasks accounted for about 85% of sampled effect sizes and showed significantly negative average synergy. Open-ended creation tasks accounted for about 10% and showed positive average synergy, significantly greater than decision-task synergy; the supplied evidence does not establish that creation-task synergy itself significantly exceeded zero. The authors advocate better integration processes, while acknowledging insufficient evidence on moderator interactions. This broader result qualifies general claims of creative complementarity rather than resolving the separate question of collective diversity.

qs.q: A Roadmap for Future Work: Finding Human-AI Synergy: Even though our main result suggests that – on average – combining humans and AI leads to performance losses, we do not think this means that combining humans and AI is a bad idea.
qs.a: When Combinations of Humans and AI Are Useful: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis · Academia · 2024

qs.q: In our broad sample of recent experiments, the vast majority (about 85%) of the effect sizes were for decision-making tasks in which subjects chose among a predefined set of options.
qs.a: When Combinations of Humans and AI Are Useful: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis · Academia · 2024

kps.k: Practical deployment should test individual quality, collective distinctiveness and longer-term effects separately.
kps.d: Wan and Kalman recommend explicit variation in prompts, perspectives and system design, alongside assessment of aided and unaided creativity over time. These remain design recommendations rather than universally validated interventions. Across the experiments, semantic embeddings measure conceptual similarity, originality classifiers capture only selected creativity dimensions, and vocabulary richness measures something different again. Short tasks, selected populations, particular models and restricted interaction limit generalisation; the P&G field setting adds professional evidence without establishing effects across occupations. Predictions about publishing-wide convergence, retraining feedback or model collapse extend beyond the outcomes tested here.

qs.q: e implication is that eﬀective human-AI collaboration requires researchers and practitioners to make their implicit assumptions about diversity, perspective, and variation explicit in their interaction design, treating AI not as an intuitive collaborator who can extract implicit unstated needs, but as a powerful tool that excels at delivering precisely what is speciﬁed.
qs.a: Diverse AI Personas Can Mitigate the Homogenization Effect in Human-AI Collaborative Ideation · Academia · 2025

vlens.an: The curated academia-and-research sources support the cluster’s principal proposition that individual creative quality and collective diversity are distinct outcomes and that generative AI can improve the former while narrowing the latter. Experimental evidence from story writing and professional product development reports performance or quality gains alongside greater semantic similarity. The common explanation is not that homogenisation is inevitable, but that outcomes depend materially on task structure, exposure mode, prompting and interaction design. Internal variation is therefore important: passive exposure in a dynamic brainstorming task increased collective diversity without changing average individual originality, while the broader meta-analysis addresses task-level human–AI synergy but does not establish any diversity effect. Wan and Kalman go further by testing diversified personas, but their low-powered results leave both mitigation and preservation of individual creativity gains unresolved. Overall, these sources support the synthesis’s conditional framing and its treatment of personas as preliminary rather than proven; they do not establish a universal quality–diversity trade-off across settings.

qs.q: However, GenAI-enabled stories are more similar to each other than stories by humans alone.
qs.a: Generative AI Enhances Individual Creativity but Reduces the Collective Diversity of Novel Content · Academia · 2024

elens.an: The curated sources for this period support the proposition’s core requirement to assess individual output quality separately from collective diversity. Doshi and Hauser provide the clearest direct evidence of the trade-off: GPT-4 starting ideas improved evaluated story novelty and usefulness while making assisted stories more similar to one another. Ashkinaze and colleagues materially qualify any claim that homogenisation is inevitable: in a passive-exposure, dynamic brainstorming design, high AI exposure increased collective diversity without changing average individual creativity. Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier supports the same analytical separation by pairing better answers among participants retaining more AI output with a distinct inquiry into cross-participant diversity, although the supplied excerpt contains no diversity result and does not establish causation from retention. The meta-analysis further indicates that outcomes depend on task and integration design, finding creation tasks more promising than predefined-choice decisions, but it does not examine collective diversity. Thus, the common basis of support is that performance gains, originality and group-level distinctiveness are different outcomes whose relationship varies by task and mode of interaction. Material variation concerns direction—AI assistance narrowed diversity in short-story co-creation but broadened it under passive exposure—as well as evidentiary reach. None of these supplied source records directly tests persona-based mitigation, so they support the proposition’s quality–diversity framing more strongly than its specific characterization of personas as preliminary mitigation.

qs.q: However, GenAI-enabled stories are more similar to each other than stories by humans alone.
qs.a: Generative AI Enhances Individual Creativity but Reduces the Collective Diversity of Novel Content · Academia · 2024

elens.an: The 2025 sources accept the proposition’s central distinction between individual output gains and collective homogenisation, and together extend it toward deployment design. The P&G field experiment supplies organisational evidence beyond story-writing: AI-assisted work improved performance while outputs became more semantically similar, although extensive retention still involved meaningful human shaping. Wan and Kalman then make a concrete design contribution by testing deliberately varied AI personas as a possible response to homogenisation. Their evidence supports purposeful diversification rather than treating convergence as inevitable, but it does not establish personas as a scalable solution: the human-story phase was underpowered, results varied by specification and exposure condition, and preservation of individual creativity gains remains untested. Material variation therefore concerns setting and evidential strength—the P&G study demonstrates the quality–similarity pattern in professional product development, whereas the persona study offers preliminary mitigation evidence in a small creative-writing experiment. These curated sources should not be read as representative of all 2025 research or deployments.
